mathematical_review.subject: Named zero-budget data and normalization
mathematical_review.finding: zeroBudgetCandidate is exactly the finite pair cutoff=0, coefficient=0. Unconditional actualKappa positivity supplies normalized moment u_0=1, degree-zero weight=1 and variation V_0=1. This alone is not cancellation C_0=0, which also involves V_1.

mathematical_review.subject: First finite row
mathematical_review.finding: The degree-one weights are 1-u_1 and u_1; V_1=|1-u_1|+|u_1|. The existing cancellation identity gives C_0=V_1-1, and the source derives C_0=0 iff 0<=u_1<=1.

mathematical_review.subject: Second finite row
mathematical_review.finding: The three degree-two weights are 1-2u_1+u_2, 2(u_1-u_2), and u_2. Unit total mass makes V_2=1 equivalent to all three weights being nonnegative, exactly u_2>=0, u_2<=u_1 and 2u_1<=1+u_2. Enumeration j=0,1,2 follows from j in range(3). With V_1=1 established, this also characterizes C_1=0.

mathematical_review.subject: Independent height bound
mathematical_review.finding: For 0<=Re(s)<=1 and |Im(s)|<=5/4, both squared norms are <=41/16, so ||s(s-1)||<=41/16. The imported unconditional bound ||completedRiemannZeta_0(s)||<=3/8 gives product norm <=123/128<1, contradicting the xi-zero equation whose product norm is 1.

mathematical_review.subject: Sector and positive real squares
mathematical_review.finding: For w=sqrt(z) at a theta zero, critical-strip membership gives |Re(w)|<1/2 and the new height bound gives |Im(w)|>5/4. The existing slope lemma with m=5/2 yields Re(z)/||z||<=-21/29. Applied to z=-actualComplexScale(i), this yields Re(scale)>=21/29*||scale||. Since 2*(21/29)^2-1=41/841>0 and scale is nonzero, Re(scale^2)>0. Complex inversion and positive real normalization preserve positivity of the real part of the squared canonical node.

mathematical_review.subject: HasSum and lower moment bound
mathematical_review.finding: canonicalPowerSums 1 supplies the exact HasSum of canonicalNode(i)^2 to u_1 cast into Complex. Taking real parts yields a real HasSum to u_1. Each real squared-node term is positive, and the imported actual divisor is nonempty; a selected term is bounded by the sum, proving u_1>0.

mathematical_review.subject: Upper moment bound
mathematical_review.finding: Positive real canonical masses sum to 1, hence each a_i=Re(canonicalNode(i)) lies in (0,1]. For b_i=Im(canonicalNode(i)), Re(canonicalNode(i)^2)=a_i^2-b_i^2<=a_i. Applying hasSum_le to the two supplied HasSum identities gives u_1<=1.
